Dynamic types, the DLR and CIL

Compare ordinary type checking with an operation checked when the program runs.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A shared toolbox and a console app that uses it

Put reusable rules in a class library, then call them from a console project. Explore how C# can inspect types or create a small type at runtime.

The example prints results in the console; it does not use a database.

Check the result

Build both projects together, run the console app and check the rule and reflection output.

var and dynamic are not the same. var asks the compiler to work out a fixed type. dynamic postpones many member checks until runtime.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Try an expandable object

dynamic student = new System.Dynamic.ExpandoObject();
student.Name = "Lefa";
Console.WriteLine(student.Name);

Expected: Lefa. A misspelled student.Nmae can fail at runtime. With var student = new { Name = "Lefa" }, Name is compiler checked and the anonymous object has a fixed read-only shape. dynamic can help with dynamic-object interoperability, but should not replace clear types in normal domain/API code.

DLR, CLR and intermediate code

C# compiles to Common Intermediate Language and metadata in an assembly. The Common Language Runtime executes managed code, often through JIT compilation; ahead-of-time compilation is another deployment option. The Dynamic Language Runtime supplies dynamic binding infrastructure and call-site caching. It does not turn dynamic into a separate database or make unknown member access safe.

Try it yourself

Choose var or dynamic for a normal Student DTO.

Worked answer

Use a named Student type (possibly held in a var local). Keep compile-time checks for routine structured data.

What does a runtime binder exception suggest?

Worked answer

A member name, argument list or runtime type did not support the requested operation. Inspect the actual value/type.

Predict and practise

Does dynamic guarantee that a requested method exists?

Check your prediction

No. Some checks happen at runtime and may fail then.

Make one change

Compare a normal call and the example dynamic call.

Worked guidance

Try a wrong member name in a separate experiment and observe the runtime failure.

Try independently

Explain a useful dynamic scenario and rewrite a simple example using a known type.
